title: Real-Time Call Assistant
subtitle: Design a call assistant that suggests within about three seconds, then drafts a reviewed summary and CRM update after the call.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Three clocks and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Sort every task by when its answer is needed and name the questions that change the design.

practice_prompts.label: Latency budget
practice_prompts.hint: Say the stage budget as arithmetic and what the headroom pays for.

practice_prompts.label: Consent, redaction and approval
practice_prompts.hint: Place each boundary and say what fails closed and what degrades.

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: Score the summary by purpose and order the launch.

rubric: I split the work into before, during and after the call, and kept the CRM and the large model out of the three-second lane.
I stated the ~2.0 s stage budget from end-of-utterance, its ~1 s headroom and that it is a planning assumption to measure.
I placed consent before recording and redaction on the stream before storage and any model call.
I showed silence on timeout and labelled degradation for a stale snapshot or missed live lookup.
I had the model propose CRM changes with evidence-based confidence and the rep approve every write through an idempotent gateway.
I evaluated summaries by purpose, with action-item precision and recall sliced by call type and language, and launched post-call first.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 November 2026: read all 44 captured sections of the real-time call assistant source and authored a teach-mode rewrite from scratch. The overview, main guide, deep dive and cheat sheet repeat the Full Design's mechanisms, so each mechanism is taught once in the place that fits (three-clock split in step 1, budget arithmetic with the explicit 2,000 ms sum in step 4, per-lane figures inside the snapshot, live-lane and post-call dives) and the shorter versions are mapped as consolidated. The brief uses the source's own Sara/Acme trace as the example and defines CRM, ASR, diarization, PII, VAD and p95 before use. Every substantive table (14 of 18; the old navigation table is consolidated, the main NFR table is merged into the fuller constraints table, and the follow-up table became eight reveals) and all 8 diagrams in both variants are kept beside their explanation. Old 'section N' pointers were removed from table cells and replaced with links to the new anchors. Three changed-constraint questions (unknown inbound caller, mid-call redaction outage, auto-applied stage) are labelled as authored additions; the consent-law example in the privacy dive comes from the source's own references. No RAG-case material was imported beyond the voice project's retrieval step the source itself describes. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained casebook: eight walkthrough steps, eight protected figures, all three lanes and stage timings, speech/transcript/CRM boundaries, privacy and retention, summary evaluation, all source questions and three changed-constraint drills. Targeted corrections and source-to-output mappings: /Users/sourav/Github_Repos/Forward-Deployed-Engineer-Interview-Prep/.website_spec/casebook-review-next-ten-2026-11-20/real-time-call-assistant/audit.json. Historical captured-source mappings remain preserved; this pass audits the maintained baseline.
